title: UZBEK AGGLUTINATIVE MORPHOLOGY VS. ENGLISH ANALYTICAL
description: This article presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of Uzbek agglutinative morphology and English analytical structure. Uzbek, as an agglutinative language, expresses grammatical categories through regular and transparent suffix sequences attached to roots, enabling compact encoding of meaning (Avalova, 2025). English, in contrast, relies on word order, auxiliary verbs, and separate function words rather than extensive morphological markers (Muhammadieva & Abdamutova, 2025). This study explores word formation, morphological and syntactic patterns, semantic distribution, and implications for language learning and translation. Findings highlight the cognitive and pedagogical challenges in cross-linguistic transfer between Uzbek and English (Akhmedov, 2024).
